newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rotterdam bunkers tick up, Mediterranean stays put.
newsitem.headline: Rotterdam bunkers tick up, Mediterranean stays put.

text.p: Rotterdam bunker prices ticked up by about $1 as short-covering lifted the barge market, while Mediterranean levels were steady, dealers said.
Rotterdam 380 CST fuel oil was quoted in the range $89/$90 fob as barges rose above $87 ex-wharf with some short covering by independent suppliers.
Total ARA business was relatively low, at around 10,000 tonnes.

Hamburg prices shot up by around $5 a tonne to $95 delivered for 380 CST material. Suppliers said the rises were a response to gains in Rotterdam. Demand was low as the rising dollar made prices appear even worse in German marks.
Mediterranean prices were unchanged and business in most ports was fairly quiet.
French ports were mostly inactive due to the Bastille Day public holiday.
In Durban, prices were broadly steady, but supplies were disrupted at the weekend when one of the underground pipelines supplying the harbour was ruptured.
Only Engen and BP are on line with supplies this week, dealers said.
